items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: I’m trying to reach the level of Coltrane and Charlie Parker and Lester Young. That’s been set, that standard of brilliance.

ctx.x: I’m not sure how to ask this but after hearing you play, which was really terrific last night, I should tell our viewers it was in Utica, New York at a cool little place called The Other Side. It seems to me you have abundant technique to play whatever you want. I’m going to go from that premise. So is the challenge not so much how to play it but what to think of? What is something tonight that I can do that I haven’t done repeatedly, and if that statement is sort of true, where do your ideas come from?

Well thank you for the kind words. It was a really cool place to play actually, The Other Side, and it was a nice gallery with art work and stuff. And then it was filled with people but with 60 — it was like packed but it’s a small place. But really, talking to people before, during the break and then afterwards really, it’s a kind of a cool thing about jazz or this improvised music is that those people were there to really hear music and they stayed, and then talking to them and just you realize that this music…

Then you have to just allow the music to happen. And that’s what’s the beautiful part about improvised music and jazz is that then you also hear the drummer do something or Ron last night playing the organ, okay the way he chorded it, or like that connection you have, the conversation. So then it’s a combination of like accepting what’s coming in, accepting what’s happening around you, and then the feeling of the room, actually when you kind of just sense the vibes from the people. There’s all that combination it…
